title: OpenStax: innate immunity is fast and nonspecific; adaptive immunity is slower and specific
summary: The textbook distinguishes barriers, a rapid innate response, and a slower adaptive response.
body: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 21.1, describes barriers to invasion, a rapid but nonspecific innate immune response, and a slower, more specific adaptive immune response controlled largely by white blood cells. NIAID's immune-system overview page was fetched but the sentences we searched did not cleanly state the cell list, so B cells, T cells, macrophages, and NK cells are not itemized from that page. The v1 list of those cells is left for a sourced anatomy card only where OpenStax's wording supports the distinction above.
